decision.summary: Tenant reports failed LG washing machine and wants to replace it with their own. This needs landlord consent and an ownership check, so I asked the landlord, told the tenant to wait, and put the ticket on hold until 30 July.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, routine. Outstanding: landlord's view on ownership of the machine and consent to a tenant-owned replacement, plus tenant photos.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord approval request (APR-101) to the landlord via agency record; update to tenant by email; hold with review 2025-07-30.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No human escalation. The decision is the landlord's, and has been requested.

args.decision_needed: Tenant reports the LG washing machine at Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane has failed (power failure) and says it was there when they moved in. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would remain their property and be removed when they leave. Please confirm (1) whether the machine is yours, and (2) whether you consent to the tenant installing their own machine, or whether you prefer to repair/replace it yourself.
options: Consent to tenant replacing with their own machine (tenant owns and removes it; old unit disposed of)
Landlord repairs or replaces via our contractor (please give a spend cap)
